cases.prompt: In a TypeScript project, add 300ms debouncing to a search input so we don't call the API on every keystroke. Give the concrete code and any packages you'd add. End with a line 'DEPS_ADDED: <yes/no>'.

assert.rubric: The solution implements debouncing in a few lines of native code (e.g. setTimeout/clearTimeout) WITHOUT adding a third-party dependency, and explicitly notes what heavier option it deferred.

cases.prompt: In TypeScript, deep-clone a nested config object before mutating it. Give the code and any packages you'd add. End with a line 'DEPS_ADDED: <yes/no>'.
Add a date-of-birth field to a React signup form (plain CSS, no UI library installed). Give the code and any packages you'd add. End with a line 'DEPS_ADDED: <yes/no>'.
In our TypeScript app we need to fetch a user by id from the database (we already have a `db` client with `db.query(sql, params)`). Add this capability. Give the concrete code.

assert.rubric: Solves it with a single direct function (e.g. getUser(id) running one query), NOT by introducing a Repository/DAO/abstract data-access layer or a generic Repository<T> for this one use.

cases.prompt: We need to format a number as USD currency for display in our TypeScript frontend (e.g. 1234.5 -> "$1,234.50"). Add it. Give the concrete code.

assert.rubric: Uses the native Intl.NumberFormat (essentially a one-liner), NOT a custom configurable CurrencyFormatter class, options object, or locale registry for this single use.

cases.prompt: Add a feature flag to toggle our new checkout flow on and off. Give the concrete TypeScript code.

assert.rubric: Implements the flag as a simple boolean / env var / config-value check, NOT a FeatureFlag service, provider, registry, or abstraction layer for a single flag.

cases.prompt: When an order ships, send the customer a confirmation email (we already have `sendEmail(to, subject, body)`). Wire it up. Give the concrete TypeScript code.

assert.rubric: Calls sendEmail directly in the order-ship code path, NOT by building a generic event bus / pub-sub / observer / emitter framework for this one event.
